headline: Lions 19, Dolphins 9

body.label: Turning points
body.text: Miami’s defense held Detroit’s top-ranked offense without a first-half touchdown, but the Dolphins missed a 38-yard field goal before halftime and opened the third quarter with a turnover. Detroit finally broke through on Jahmyr Gibbs’ fourth-down touchdown, taking a 16–6 lead.

body.label: Standouts
body.text: Rookie Chris Johnson intercepted Jared Goff, Jordyn Brooks made 12 tackles, and Josh Uche, Zeek Biggers and Jacob Rodriguez each recorded a sack. Caleb Douglas led Miami with six catches for 70 yards.

body.label: Injury/roster news
body.text: Malik Willis said his lingering groin injury felt tight; he finished with only seven rushing yards. Tight end Will Kacmarek sustained a quadriceps injury but walked off unassisted.

body.label: Takeaway
body.text: The defense gave Miami every opportunity, limiting Detroit to 271 yards. The offense squandered it by going 0-for-3 in the red zone, committing 11 penalties and producing just 228 yards. That imbalance is now Miami’s defining problem.

next: At Indianapolis Colts — Sunday, Nov 15, 1:00 PM ET on CBS

hurricanes.headline: No. 4 Notre Dame 31, No. 1 Miami 24

body.label: Turning points
body.text: Miami fell behind 24–3 before Darian Mensah led a determined second-half comeback. The decisive sequence came after the Hurricanes pulled within 24–17: Luke Talich intercepted Mensah, and Notre Dame converted the turnover into a touchdown. Miami’s final serious drive ended when Talich broke up a potential game-tying fourth-down touchdown to Elija Lofton.

body.label: Standouts
body.text: Mensah completed 24 of 43 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns, with one interception. Cooper Barkate caught 10 passes for 92 yards and two scores; Lofton added seven receptions for 113 yards and a touchdown.

body.label: Injury/roster news
body.text: Star receiver Malachi Toney missed the game with an ankle injury requiring surgery, a major loss for Miami’s passing attack. Starting guard Max Buchanan and cornerback O.J. Frederique also remained unavailable. The official postgame recap identified no significant new injury.

body.label: Takeaway
body.text: Miami’s 21–14 second-half response showed real resilience, but the slow start, goal-line failure and poorly timed interception proved too costly. The loss damages the Hurricanes’ playoff margin, though their ACC objectives remain intact.

hurricanes.next: Duke at Miami on Saturday, November 14, at noon ET on ABC.
